mainTopic: Does each sage learn one law of offerings from another? רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן and רב on making a מנחה (and the חביתין) holy in halves, plus רב's rule on oil and לבונה
overview: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר does not apply his rule about דם to the חביתין of the כהן גדול. It answers that he learns a מנחה only from another מנחה, never from דם. It then tests that answer with a ברייתא about לחם הפנים that broke, and defends רבי אלעזר: the לבונה is already set apart in its bowls, and he holds the קומץ is burned even when the שירים become lacking. Next the גמרא returns to the main dispute. רבי יוחנן says the חביתין cannot become holy in halves, based on the פסוק 'מנחה מחציתה'. רבי אלעזר says they can. רבי אלעזר is defended against a ברייתא and the word 'חוקה'. רבי יוחנן is defended by the rule that someone who plans to add more flour is a special case. The גמרא concludes that רב must hold like רבי יוחנן. Finally it quotes רב's rule in full: a מנחה becomes holy without its oil or לבונה, and oil and לבונה each become holy without the other. The amud ends as a statement of רבי חנינא begins, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not learn this from blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. If his rule about דם is true, he should apply the same rule to the מנחה being discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that is so, let him learn it from blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר does not take the rule he holds about דם and apply it to the חביתין of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said that רבי אלעזר holds that blood cannot be made holy in halves. If he holds that about blood, the same logic should work for the מנחה. The question is why he does not make that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is so; if that is really his view
Let him learn (derive) it
The blood of a קרבן

phrases.english: And if it is so, let him derive it from blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי אלעזר's view on blood not being made holy in halves.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's failure to apply his blood rule to the מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since he holds the rule about blood, consistency demands he learn the מנחה from blood too.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that he never compares topics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a possible defense: maybe רבי אלעזר never learns one topic from another. It rejects this right away by showing that he does compare a מנחה to the בזיכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that רבי אלעזר does not learn one matter from another matter: but רבי אלעזר said that a מנחה whose handful was taken in the היכל is valid, because we find something similar with the removal of the בזיכין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a defense for רבי אלעזר and then knocks it down by quoting another ruling of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible defense is that רבי אלעזר simply does not use comparisons. But he rules that קמיצה done in the היכל is valid, and he learns this from the בזיכין, which are removed in the היכל. So he clearly does learn one case from another, and the original question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא raises a possible answer)
One matter from another matter
Took a handful (קמיצה) from the מנחה
The Sanctuary building, inside, past the courtyard
Removing the two bowls of frankincense from the Table of לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not give רבי אלעזר's answer. The גמרא raises a defense only to reject it, so the question from step 1 still stands.

phrases.english: And if you would say: Rabbi Elazar
does not derive one matter from another matter?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
A meal offering whose handful he removed in the Sanctuary is valid,
for we find this with the removal of the bowls of frankincense.
phrases.notes: The bowls are taken off the Table inside the Sanctuary, and that permits the bread. So taking a handful inside can work too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִילְּתָא מִמִּילְּתָא לָא גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Anticipates a defense against step 1 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested defense that רבי אלעזר never derives one matter from another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר himself learns קמיצה in the היכל from סילוק בזיכין, so he does use comparisons.

steps.title: A meal offering from a meal offering, but not from blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רבי אלעזר compares a מנחה to another מנחה (the לחם הפנים counts as one), but he does not compare a מנחה to דם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns a מנחה from a מנחה. He does not learn a מנחה from blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 1 by limiting which comparisons רבי אלעזר will make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בזיכין case works because the לחם הפנים is also a kind of מנחה, so it is a close match. דם is a different kind of offering, so רבי אלעזר will not learn the חביתין from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering, made of flour
He derives / learns

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי אלעזר compares like with like: a מנחה only to another מנחה, not to דם.

phrases.english: He derives a meal offering from a meal offering,
he does not derive a meal offering from blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחָה מִמִּנְחָה יָלֵיף, מִנְחָה מִדָּם לָא יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between same-category and cross-category derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אלעזר derives from בזיכין, he should also derive from דם.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only derives within the category of מנחות; דם is a different category.

steps.title: Does he really compare one meal offering to another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer. It brings a ברייתא about לחם הפנים that broke before or after being taken off the Table.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he derive a מנחה from a מנחה? But a ברייתא teaches: if the bread broke before he took it off, the bread is invalid, and he does not burn the בזיכין for it. If the bread broke after he took it off, the bread is invalid, but he does burn the בזיכין for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins attacking the answer from step 3 by quoting a ברייתא. The full point of the attack becomes clear after רבי אלעזר's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the timing of the removal from the Table decide whether the frankincense is still burned. If the bread broke before removal, the frankincense is not burned. If it broke after removal, it is burned even though the bread itself is invalid. The גמרא will use this to test whether רבי אלעזר is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it apart / removed the arrangement from the Table
Broke into pieces
Invalid
Burns on the מזבח

phrases.english: And does he derive a meal offering from a meal offering?
But isn't it taught: Before he detached it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the arrangement of shewbread and the bowls, taken off the Table.

phrases.english: if its bread broke, the bread is invalid,
and he does not burn the bowls of frankincense on its account.
If after he detached it, its bread broke,
the bread is invalid,
but he does burn the bowls of frankincense on its account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר derives a מנחה from a מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about broken לחם הפנים, as רבי אלעזר explains it, will be used to show a problem with that claim.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: once the time comes, it counts as removed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the ברייתא. Detaching does not mean physically taking it off. Once the time to detach arrives, the bread is treated as already detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: not actually detached. Rather, once the time to detach it has arrived, even if he did not detach it, it is as if he detached it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's reading of the ברייתא. This sets up the challenge to step 3, which comes next in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the time for removal matters, not the physical act. So if the bread breaks after that time, the frankincense is still burned. The גמרא will use this view to test whether he really learns a מנחה from a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, physically
Its time has arrived
It is considered as if...

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished yet. רבי אלעזר's statement is the setup; the גמרא draws out the actual difficulty right after this.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא פֵּרְקָהּ מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: Not that he actually detached it,
rather, once its time to be detached has arrived,
even though he did not detach it,
it is considered as though he detached it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא פֵּרְקָהּ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי אלעזר's reading of the ברייתא to build the challenge begun in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the time for removing the לחם הפנים arrives, it is treated as removed, even without physical removal.

steps.title: Why not treat the broken bread like a meal offering that lost some before the handful was taken?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אלעזר compares one מנחה to another, the bread breaking on the Table should be like a מנחה that became lacking before קמיצה, where nothing is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should the frankincense be burned? The case should be like a meal offering that became short before the handful was taken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's reading of the ברייתא. If the לחם הפנים broke while still on the Table, it should be just like a מנחה that became lacking before קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3 we said רבי אלעזר does compare one מנחה to another. A regular מנחה that loses some of its amount before the קמיצה cannot have its קומץ burned. So the לבונה of a לחם הפנים that broke before being taken off the Table should not be burned either.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן taking a handful out of a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
A meal offering that became short of its required amount
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And why?
phrases.notes: Why should the frankincense be burned when the bread broke while still on the Table, as in the ברייתא from Step 4?

phrases.english: Let it be like a meal offering
that became lacking before the handful was taken!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? תֶּיהְוֵי כְּמִנְחָה שֶׁחָסְרָה קוֹדֶם קְמִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's explanation from Step 5, using his own method of comparing one מנחה to another.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the לבונה is burned once the time to detach has arrived.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מנחה that is lacking before קמיצה cannot be offered. The לחם הפנים is like a מנחה, so if it broke before detaching, its לבונה should not be offered either.

steps.title: The frankincense of the showbread is already clearly set apart
steps.stepSummary: In a regular מנחה the קומץ is not yet separate, but the לבונה of the לחם הפנים sits in its own bowls, so once the time to detach comes, it counts as detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. In a regular meal offering, the handful is not yet clearly set apart. Here, the handful is already clearly set apart. So once the time to detach arrives, it is as if it was already detached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a real difference between a regular מנחה and the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a regular מנחה, the קומץ is mixed into the flour until the כהן takes it out, so a shortage before קמיצה ruins everything. With the לחם הפנים, the 'handful' is the לבונה, which is already in separate bowls. Since it is already set apart, the rule that 'time to detach = detached' can work here.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearly identified or set apart
To detach, here meaning taking the bread and bowls off the Table
It is considered as though it was already detached

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
a meal offering, its handful was not clearly set apart,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Both words mean the same thing anyway.

phrases.english: but here, its handful was clearly set apart,
phrases.notes: Here the 'handful' means the frankincense, which sits in its own bowls.

phrases.english: and once its time to detach has arrived,
it is as if someone already detached it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לחם הפנים is just like any מנחה that became lacking before קמיצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לבונה of the לחם הפנים is already set apart, so the time to detach counts as detaching. This is unlike a regular מנחה, where the קומץ is not yet separate.

steps.title: Then treat it like leftovers that became lacking before the burning
steps.stepSummary: Even if it counts as detached, the bread broke before the לבונה was burned. That should be like שירים that became lacking between קמיצה and הקטרה, where the קומץ is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, let it be like leftovers that became lacking between the taking of the handful and the burning, where we do not burn the handful for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the answer for now but raises a new challenge. Even if the bread counts as detached, it still broke before the לבונה was burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treat the time to detach as if the קמיצה already happened. Even so, the bread breaking is like the שירים becoming lacking after the קמיצה but before the הקטרה. The גמרא assumes that in such a case the קומץ is not burned, so the לבונה here should not be burned either.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: taking your answer to its next step to raise a problem
The leftover part of a מנחה after the קומץ is taken out
Burning the קומץ on the מזבח

phrases.english: But if so,
let it be like leftovers that became lacking
between taking the handful and burning it,
where we do not burn the handful on their account!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of Step 7 and challenges it again.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the time to detach counts as detaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even after the detaching, the bread broke before the burning. That is like שירים that became lacking before הקטרה, and in that case the קומץ is not burned.

steps.title: It is a dispute, and רבי אלעזר holds the handful is burned
steps.stepSummary: Whether the קומץ is burned when the שירים became lacking before הקטרה is a dispute. רבי אלעזר follows the view that it is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a dispute? רבי אלעזר holds like the one who says that if the leftovers became lacking between the taking of the handful and the burning, the handful is still burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule used in the challenge is not agreed on by everyone. רבי אלעזר simply holds the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a shortage between קמיצה and הקטרה stops the burning. In fact, this is a disagreement, and one view says the קומץ is still burned. רבי אלעזר follows that view, so his ruling about the לבונה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute between sages
Following the view of the sage who says...

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's position holds up: the לבונה is already set apart, the time to detach counts as detaching, and he holds that a shortage after the קמיצה does not stop the burning.

phrases.english: Isn't it a dispute?
Rabbi Elazar holds
like the one who says:
leftovers that became lacking between taking the handful and burning it,
he burns the handful on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the rule is disputed, and the sage holds the other view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that a shortage between קמיצה and הקטרה stops the burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a dispute, and רבי אלעזר holds the קומץ is still burned.

steps.title: Back to the dispute: is the High Priest's griddle-cake offering sanctified in halves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main dispute. רבי יוחנן says the חביתי כהן גדול cannot become holy one half at a time. רבי אלעזר says it can, since it is offered in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself: about the griddle cakes of the כהן גדול, רבי יוחנן says it is not sanctified in halves. רבי אלעזר says: since it is offered in halves, it is sanctified in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to the original dispute that came up earlier. It now states that dispute in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתי כהן גדול is offered half in the morning and half in the afternoon. רבי אלעזר reasons that because it is offered in halves, it can also become holy in halves. רבי יוחנן says it must become holy as one whole.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to a statement mentioned earlier in order to discuss it
The daily griddle-cake מנחה brought by the כהן גדול
Becomes holy one half at a time
Since, because of

phrases.english: The matter itself:
the griddle cakes of the High Priest,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
it is not sanctified in halves,
and Rabbi Elazar says:
since it is offered in halves,
it is sanctified in halves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the original dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the חביתי כהן גדול is not sanctified in halves. רבי אלעזר: it is sanctified in halves, since it is offered in halves.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא explains that רבי יוחנן learns from the פסוק 'a meal offering, half of it': first bring a whole מנחה, and only then divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא said: What is רבי יוחנן's reason? The verse says 'a meal offering, half of it.' This means: bring a whole meal offering, and afterward divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא gives the source from the פסוק for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'a meal offering' and only then 'half of it.' רבי יוחנן reads this as an order: the מנחה must first be made holy as a whole, and only afterward is it split. That is why it cannot become holy half at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Half of it

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan?
The verse states: "A meal offering, half of it,"
bring a meal offering, and afterward divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the פסוק for רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the חביתי כהן גדול is not sanctified in halves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'מנחה מחציתה' (ויקרא 6:13): first a whole מנחה, then dividing it.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the חביתין must come from a whole עשרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. A משנה and ברייתא say the כהן גדול brings a full עשרון and then divides it. He does not bring separate halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: The חביתין of the כהן גדול did not come in halves. Rather, he brings a full עשרון and divides it. And a ברייתא teaches: If the פסוק had only said 'a מנחה, half,' I would have said he brings half an עשרון from home in the morning and offers it, and half an עשרון from home in the evening and offers it. So the פסוק says 'half of it in the morning': he brings a half taken from a whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to go against רבי אלעזר, who said the חביתין can become holy one half at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'מחציתה' (half of IT) to mean the half must come out of a whole. If the half must come from a whole עשרון, it seems you cannot make just a half holy. That clashes with רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake מנחה of the כהן גדול, offered half in the morning and half in the evening
A tenth of an איפה, the standard measure of flour for a מנחה
Halves
A half taken out of a whole
The פסוק comes to teach

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לֹא הָיוּ בָּאוֹת חֲצָאִין,
phrases.english: The griddle-cakes of the High Priest did not come in halves,
rather, he brings a full tenth and divides it;
and it is taught: If it had said 'a meal offering, half,'

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: מֵבִיא חֲצִי עִשָּׂרוֹן מִבֵּיתוֹ
phrases.english: I would have said: he brings half a tenth from his home
in the morning and offers it,
and half a tenth from his home in the evening and offers it;
therefore the verse says: 'half of it in the morning' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13. The extra letter ה ('of it') points back to a whole.

phrases.english: he brings a half from a whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's side of the dispute from Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר, who said the חביתין can become holy in halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the half to come from a whole עשרון, so making a half holy by itself seems wrong.

steps.title: The whole עשרון is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ברייתא is describing the best way to do the מצוה, not what is required after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the מצוה (the ideal way).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר with one word: the requirement of a whole עשרון is only the ideal way to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally a whole עשרון is brought and divided. After the fact, if only a half was made holy, it still works. So the ברייתא does not contradict רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The ideal way to do it from the start, but not required after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does not mean the rule is unimportant. It means you should do it this way, but the offering is still valid if you did not.

phrases.english: It is for the מצוה (ideally).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to the ideal way, not a requirement after the fact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a half on its own can never become holy
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole עשרון is only the ideal; after the fact a half can become holy

steps.title: The word חוקה should make the detail required
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהא asks רב אשי: the Torah calls the חביתין a 'חוקה,' and that word normally means every detail is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהא מבי כתיל said to רב אשי: But 'חוקה' is written about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer of 'למצוה' is attacked. The Torah uses the word 'חוקה' about the חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah calls something a חוקה, its details are required, not just ideal. So bringing a whole עשרון should be required even after the fact, and the answer of Step 13 looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Statute.' A word that signals the details of a מצוה are required

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָא מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Katil said to Rav Ashi:
But 'statute' is written about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'למצוה' answer of Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a whole עשרון is only the ideal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'חוקה' makes details required, so the whole עשרון should be required too.

steps.title: חוקה refers only to bringing a whole עשרון from home
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the word חוקה only requires bringing a whole עשרון from home. It does not require making the whole amount holy at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was needed only to require bringing it whole from his home.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows what the word 'חוקה' applies to, which saves רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate stages. One is bringing the flour from home. The other is making it holy in a כלי שרת. The חוקה requirement covers the first stage: a whole עשרון must come from home. Making it holy can still happen one half at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for
From his home, before the flour enters a holy vessel

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי אלעזר: a whole עשרון must be brought from home (חוקה), but the flour can become holy one half at a time.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was needed only
to require bringing it whole from his home.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לַהֲבִיאָהּ שָׁלֵם מִבֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Rav Geviha's challenge in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the word חוקה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חוקה makes every detail required, including making the whole amount holy together
steps.terutzMaskana: חוקה only requires a whole עשרון from home; making it holy can happen in halves

steps.title: רבי יוחנן elsewhere says a half עשרון does become holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges רבי יוחנן. In another case he ruled that a half עשרון set aside with plans to add more does become holy. Why did he not learn the opposite from the חביתין?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But it was stated: If someone set aside half an עשרון and planned to add more, רב says it is not holy and רבי יוחנן says it is holy. And if he holds the חביתין cannot become holy in halves, let him learn from the חביתין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רבי יוחנן said the חביתין cannot become holy one half at a time. But in the case of a regular מנחה, he says a half does become holy. If he held a half of the חביתין cannot become holy, he should have applied the same rule to other מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside for an offering
And he plans to add more later
Becomes holy
Let him learn (derive) it

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But it was stated: If one set aside half a tenth,
and his plan is to add more –
Rav says: it is not holy,
and Rabbi Yochanan says: it is holy.
And if so, let him learn from the griddle-cakes!
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי יוחנן holds the חביתין can't become holy in halves, he should rule the same way for any מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבי אלעזר to challenging רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the חביתין cannot become holy in halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He rules a half עשרון of another מנחה becomes holy. If he really held the חביתין rule, he should have learned from it and ruled the opposite.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן does learn one case from another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: that רבי יוחנן never learns one case from another. He does exactly that with שלמים slaughtered in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי יוחנן does not learn one matter from another, but רבי יוחנן said: שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are valid, as it is written 'and he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד,' so that the secondary area should not be stricter than the main area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a possible defense of רבי יוחנן and knocks it down right away, so the challenge of Step 16 still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the courtyard as the place to slaughter שלמים. Even so, רבי יוחנן allows slaughtering them in the more important היכל, because the lesser place cannot be stricter than the main one. He is learning the היכל's law from the courtyard, so he clearly does learn one case from another.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn one matter from another matter
Peace offerings
The Sanctuary building, holier than the courtyard
The secondary or lesser thing (here, the courtyard)
The main thing (here, the היכל)

steps.confusionAlert: Here, 'אהל מועד' itself means the היכל. 'The entrance of the אהל מועד' is the courtyard in front of it.

phrases.english: And if you will say that Rabbi Yochanan
does not learn one matter from another matter,
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
peace offerings that were slaughtered in the Sanctuary are valid,
as it is written: 'and he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,'
so that the secondary should not be stricter than the main.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִילְּתָא מִמִּילְּתָא לָא יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible answer to Step 16, which strengthens that challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that רבי יוחנן never learns one matter from another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן learns the law of the היכל from the courtyard, so he does learn one case from another, and he should have learned from the חביתין.

steps.title: Planning to add more flour is a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן does learn from the חביתין. But when a person plans to add more flour, a ברייתא of רבי יוסי teaches that each bit becomes holy as it goes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case where he plans to add is different. A ברייתא teaches that 'full' means a complete עשרון. רבי יוסי said this applies only when he does not plan to add more. If he does plan to add, each bit becomes holy as soon as it goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 16-17. רבי יוחנן's ruling about a half עשרון meant to be added to is based on a special source, not on the חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן really does learn from the חביתין that a מנחה is not made holy in halves. That rule only covers someone who has no plan to add. רבי יוסי's ברייתא shows that when a person plans to add, each part becomes holy right away, so the two rulings do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: his intention is to add more
is different
full: the word in the פסוק used to require a complete measure
each first part becomes holy as it is put in

phrases.english: Where his intention is to add, it is different,
as it is taught: 'Full' —
'full' means only complete measures
(that is to say, it is not holy
until there is a complete עשרון)
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: When does this apply?
When his intention is not to add,
but when his intention is to add —
each first part becomes holy.
phrases.notes: He means each bit of flour becomes holy the moment it enters the כלי, without waiting for the full amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רבי יוחנן raised in Steps 16-17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (an intention to add is a special exception backed by a ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a half עשרון becomes holy seems to contradict what he learns from the חביתין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does learn from the חביתין. The intention-to-add case is an exception, taught by רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: if רבי יוחנן's view is now clear, what does רב hold?

steps.title: Which view does רב hold about the חביתין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רב follows on the חביתין. If he holds like רבי אלעזר, he should learn from them that every מנחה can become holy in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב: about the חביתין, whose view does he hold? If he holds like רבי אלעזר, let him learn from the חביתין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from רבי יוחנן to רב and challenges him. רב holds that a regular מנחה does not become holy in halves, even when the person plans to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that the חביתין can become holy in halves. If רב agreed with him, he should copy that rule onto all מנחות. Yet רב rules the opposite for regular מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: like whom does he hold?
let him learn (one case from another)
the כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering

phrases.english: And Rav, regarding the חביתין,
whose view does he hold?
If like Rabbi Elazar,
let him learn from the חביתין!
phrases.notes: He means: learn that all מנחות can become holy in halves, the way רבי אלעזר says the חביתין can.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of question to רב that was just answered for רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a regular מנחה is not made holy in halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב held like רבי אלעזר that the חביתין can be made holy in halves, he should apply that rule to all מנחות. His ruling says the opposite.

steps.title: רב does learn one מנחה from another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the answer that רב never learns one case from another. רב himself learns that a מנחה becomes holy without oil or לבונה from other מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say רב does not learn one case from another: didn't רב say that a מנחה becomes holy without oil, as we see with the לחם הפנים? Without לבונה, as we see with the מנחת נסכים. Without oil and without לבונה, as we see with the מנחת חוטא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off a way to escape the question on רב. It shows that רב does learn one מנחה from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might answer that רב simply does not learn from other cases. But רב rules that a regular מנחה becomes holy in the כלי even before its oil or לבונה is added. He proves this from other מנחות that never have oil, לבונה, or both. So he does learn one case from another.

keyTerms.meaning: one matter from another matter
frankincense
the showbread, which has no oil
the flour offering brought with wine libations, which has no לבונה
a poor sinner's flour offering, which has no oil or לבונה

phrases.english: And if you will say
Rav does not learn one matter from another,
but didn't Rav say:
A מנחה becomes holy without oil
(and without frankincense) —
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets. That fits better, since the לחם הפנים only proves the 'without oil' part.

phrases.english: as we find with the showbread.
Without frankincense —
as we find with the flour offering of the libations.
Without oil and without frankincense —
as we find with the sinner's flour offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַב מִילְּתָא מִמִּילְּתָא לָא יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as Step 17: it blocks the escape that this sage never learns one case from another.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of רב: that he never learns one case from another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own ruling about oil and לבונה learns one מנחה from other מנחות, so the defense fails.

steps.title: רב must hold like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Since רב does learn from other cases, he must hold like רבי יוחנן that the חביתין are not made holy in halves. That fits his rule for all מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are forced to say that רב holds like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the question on רב. He must agree with רבי יוחנן about the חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does learn from other cases, so he would follow whatever rule he holds for the חביתין. His ruling that a regular מנחה is not made holy in halves only makes sense if he holds like רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן says the חביתין are not made holy in halves.

keyTerms.meaning: necessarily; you are forced to say

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and רב both learn from the חביתין that a מנחה is not made holy in halves. רבי יוחנן makes an exception when the person plans to add, based on רבי יוסי. רב makes no such exception.

phrases.english: Necessarily,
Rav holds like Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּרְחָיךְ רַב כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question from Step 19 after Step 20 blocked the other way out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: About the חביתין, רב holds like רבי יוחנן: they are not made holy in halves, and he learns the same rule for all מנחות.

steps.title: A meal offering becomes holy even without its oil or frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's statement itself: a מנחה becomes holy without oil, without לבונה, or without both. Each point is proven from another offering that comes that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רב says: a meal offering becomes holy without its oil. Missing oil is not like missing part of the flour, because we find this with the showbread. It also becomes holy without its frankincense, because we find this with the meal offering brought with libations. It even becomes holy without both oil and frankincense, because we find this with the sinner's meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes, in full, the statement of רב that it mentioned earlier. רב rules that a מנחה can become holy even when its oil or לבונה is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If part of the flour is missing (עשרון חסר), the מנחה is not complete and does not become holy. רב says missing oil or לבונה is different, because other מנחות, like לחם הפנים, מנחת נסכים and מנחת חוטא, are normally brought without them and still become holy. This is the 'learning one case from another' that step 20 pointed to.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא goes back to quote a statement mentioned earlier in full
A tenth-measure of flour that is missing some of its flour, so it is incomplete
The showbread, made without oil
The meal offering brought with an animal offering's libations; it has no לבונה
The sinner's meal offering, brought with no oil and no לבונה

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the oil and לבונה are unimportant for the offering. He is only saying the flour can become holy in the vessel before they are added.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source step 20 referred to. It shows that רב does learn one kind of מנחה from another, which forced the conclusion that he holds like רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: The matter itself: רב says:
A meal offering becomes holy without its oil,
and its law is not like a tenth-measure that is missing,
for so we find with the showbread.
Without frankincense,
for so we find with the meal offering of libations.
Without oil and without frankincense,
for so we find with the meal offering of a sinner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to quote in full the statement of רב that was cited in step 20 and used in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה becomes holy in the vessel even without its oil, without its לבונה, or without both, as shown by לחם הפנים, מנחת נסכים and מנחת חוטא.

steps.title: Oil and frankincense each become holy on their own
steps.stepSummary: רב continues: oil and לבונה can each become holy without the other. Oil is proven from the מצורע's לוג of oil, and לבונה from the לבונה in the bowls. Then the גמרא introduces a statement of רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And oil and frankincense each become holy, this one without that one and that one without this one. Oil, because we find this with the מצורע's לוג of oil. Frankincense, because we find this with the frankincense that comes in the bowls. And רבי חנינא says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a second rule: oil and לבונה do not need each other to become holy in a vessel. The last line sets up a statement of רבי חנינא that continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 was about the flour becoming holy without its extras. Here the question is the extras themselves: can oil become holy without לבונה, and the other way around? רב proves yes, since the מצורע's לוג of oil is holy alone, and the לבונה in the בזיכין of the לחם הפנים is holy with no oil.

keyTerms.meaning: They become holy
This one without that one
The measure of oil a healed מצורע brings, holy by itself
The bowls of לבונה placed with the לחם הפנים

steps.whatToRemember: רב's full rule: the flour of a מנחה becomes holy without oil or לבונה, and oil and לבונה each become holy without the other. Every point is learned from another offering that comes that way.

phrases.english: And oil and frankincense become holy,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בְּלָא הַאי וְהַאי בְּלָא הַאי;
phrases.english: this one without that one, and that one without this one.
Oil: for so we find
with the log of oil of a leper.
Frankincense: for so we find
with the frankincense that comes in the bowls.
And רבי חנינא says:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה קׇדְשִׁי הַאי בְּלָא הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's statement, moving from the flour to the oil and לבונה themselves. It ends by introducing רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil and לבונה each become holy in a vessel without the other, as shown by the מצורע's לוג of oil and the לבונה in the בזיכין.
